Source. After `identify()` has matched the Rollei signature and `parse_rollei()` has rewound the stream to offset 0, this `fgets` macro expands to `ifp->gets(line, 128)`. It asks the datastream to materialize the first metadata line into stack `line[128]`; the staged witness is 127 bytes long and has no `\n`, so the call will run to EOF.

The callee aliases the source to the beginning of the attacker-controlled buffer and the destination to the caller's stack array. On this call `streampos == 0` because `parse_rollei()` just sought to the start, and `streamsize == 127` because the staged PoC length was stored when `open_buffer()` wrapped the witness in `LibRaw_buffer_datastream`.

Root cause. The copy bound allows `pdest` to advance while `(pdest - str) < sz` instead of stopping at `sz - 1` to preserve room for a terminator. Because the witness contains no newline, the loop exits only when `psrc` reaches EOF at `streamsize == 127`, leaving `pdest - str == 127` and `pdest` already positioned at the last in-bounds slot of `line[128]`.

After step 3, the post-loop guard still evaluates `127 < 128` as true. It checks only the current offset and does not account for the next statement's preincrement, so it approves a terminator write even though `pdest` already points at the final in-bounds byte of `line`.

Sink. `++pdest` moves from `line + 127` to `line + 128`, and the store writes one byte past `parse_rollei()`'s 128-byte stack buffer. AddressSanitizer reports `WRITE of size 1` at this statement and ties the overflow to local object `line` in the caller frame.
